To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose an optimization framework to deploy the controllers and map switches to controllers in software defined networks (SDNs).

we propose optimization models for deploying controllers and assigning switches to controllers in a resilient manner while achieving a minimum cost, minimum backup capacity, minimum latency or a combination of them.

the proposed models can achieve at least 30% reduction in the total number of required controllers, at least 50-60% reduction in the required backup capacity, and at least 50 percent reduction in the coefficient of variation with the existing approaches.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the controller placement problem with resilience to a pre-scheduled number of controller failures, and the minimum backup capacity reserved at the controllers while fixing the number of controllers.

improving the controller placement in SDN with minimum extra backup capacity and minimum number of controllers while ensuring resilience against a pre-defined number of controller failures and a low coefficient of variation with regard to the switch to controller latency.
the problem of controller placement with resilience against controller failure in SDN.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our proposed model is more resilient and efficient than the existing approaches in the literature.
the proposed models are able to reduce the number of controllers, the backup capacity, and the switch to controller latency while maintaining a higher resilience against the controller failures.

the proposed models can achieve a lower cost and a higher resilience against failures with respect to the number of controllers and the backup capacity reserved at each controller, while achieving a lower latency and a better latency distribution with respect to the switch to controller latency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose models to minimize the number of controllers required for a network while ensuring resilience against controller failures, and models to minimize the backup capacity required to be reserved for a network while fixing the number of controllers.
our proposed models achieve a higher resilience with lower cost, lower backup capacity and lower latency when compared to existing approaches.
our proposed models are more efficient in terms of resilience against controller failures, backup capacity and latency.

it is possible to deploy a smaller number of controllers while maintaining the same level of resilience as the existing approaches.

the proposed models achieve a better performance when compared to the exiting approaches in terms of cost and resilience against controller failures while achieving the same level of performance with respect to latency.
